rationale: This is essentially Desai-Rajan-Sloan (2004) CFO/P — the published construct shown to subsume both value and accruals — and the two rank components share `oancf`, so the composite double-counts cash flow rather than combining two independent channels.

The internal logic and expected sign are consistent, but "value premium concentrated in low-accrual/high-cash-conversion firms" is a well-documented double sort, and a rank product is nearly monotone in a rank sum, so it adds little beyond proposal 1 beyond a cosmetic functional-form change.

The stated mechanism ("neutralizing cheap-and-accrual-heavy firms at zero") contradicts what the expression does — since BM is almost always positive, all gated-off firms fall to the bottom of the cross-section, making the short leg a pure accrual-heavy portfolio irrespective of valuation, plus the huge mass point at zero destabilizes quantile breakpoints.

A coherent, single-ratio construction with an independent balance-sheet measurement path, but EBITDA minus working-capital accrual is approximately pre-tax, pre-interest operating cash flow, so it is economically close to CFO/P, and dividing an unlevered flow by levered equity market cap (rather than EV) injects a leverage tilt that should be acknowledged.

Sign conventions on `recch`/`invch` are handled correctly and the sales-yield-plus-cash-conversion pairing is a reasonably distinct measurement route, but these cash-flow-statement line items are missing for a large share of firm-years and COALESCE-to-zero silently assigns those firms a median-ish quality rank, so coverage and the composition of the extreme buckets need checking.

Using accrual *instability* rather than accrual level is the most genuinely distinct idea in this batch and is internally consistent, though it must be verified that VOL's 5-period window spans five fiscal years (not five months of stale annual data), and the accrual-volatility leg may partly proxy known earnings-volatility/idiosyncratic-risk effects.
